title: Russian Railways • Enterprise Communicator UX
subtitle: Designing a component-driven interaction system under legacy constraints

facts.label: scope
facts.value: UX/UI restructuring of multi-step operational workflows and introduction of a minimal component system within a legacy application

facts.label: audience
facts.value: Internal employees performing repeatable operational tasks, where speed, accuracy, and predictability are critical

facts.label: role
facts.value: Product Designer responsible for structuring UX behavior, defining reusable components, and introducing a scalable interaction model

facts.label: focus
facts.value: Transition from fragmented UI patterns to a component-driven UX layer enabling consistent task execution

value.text:
The product is an internal enterprise tool used for executing operational workflows.

Over time, the interface evolved without a governing system:

items: UI patterns were duplicated instead of reused
interaction logic varied across similar tasks

value.text: A UI kit existed in fragments, but there was no real design system:
At the same time, the system operated under heavy legacy constraints:

items: high cost of breaking existing behavior

value.text: The product functioned, but its UX layer became increasingly inefficient to use and scale.
The interface lacked interaction consistency, directly impacting operational performance.

items: identical tasks behaved differently across contexts
users reinterpreted UI instead of executing known actions
lack of predictability slowed down repetitive workflows

value.text:
This was not a usability issue.

It was a breakdown of interaction logic in a system where repeatability defines efficiency.

items: Core logic locked by legacy backend
No mature design system to extend
Changes had to be incremental and non-breaking

value.text: The solution had to be:

In enterprise systems, UX quality is defined by execution reliability.

Users do not explore — they execute.

A component-driven approach is the only scalable way to achieve this.
